about.seoDescription: Quick facts and an overview of the Municipality of Taal, Batangas.
about.title: About Taal
about.subtitle: Discover the Heritage Town of Batangas, home of the balisong and the Barong Tagalog, between Taal Lake and Balayan Bay.
about.photoNote: Photo placeholder: Taal heritage town center

geography.title: Geography
geography.text: A coastal municipality in Batangas, facing Balayan Bay and about 79 km south of Metro Manila.

population.title: Population
population.text: Home to 61,460 people as of the 2020 Census of Population and Housing.

heritage.title: Heritage Town
heritage.text: Its poblacion is a National Historical Landmark, with hundreds of Spanish-era structures.

landscape.title: Landscape
landscape.text: Set between Taal Lake and Balayan Bay, linked by the Pansipit River.

barangays.title: Barangays
barangays.text: 42 barangays, including 14 poblacion barangays in the town center.

paragraphs: Taal is a coastal municipality in the province of Batangas, in the CALABARZON region. Founded by Augustinian friars in 1572, it is one of the oldest towns in Batangas and once served as the provincial capital.

The town moved to its present site overlooking Balayan Bay after the great eruption of Taal Volcano in 1754. Today its town center keeps a Spanish-era grid of narrow streets, ancestral houses and the Basilica de San Martin de Tours.

Taal is known as the balisong and Barong Tagalog capital of the Philippines. Its embroidery, crafts and food, from tapang Taal to sinaing na tulingan, are celebrated every April at the El Pasubat Festival.

history.seoDescription: A timeline of Taal, Batangas from its founding in 1572 to today.
history.title: History of Taal
history.subtitle: Journey through more than 450 years of the town that was once the capital of Batangas and gave the nation its first flag.
history.photoNote: Photo placeholder: Basilica de San Martin de Tours

2020.title: Taal Volcano Eruption
2020.description: The town was evacuated for several weeks in early 2020. Ashfall and volcanic tremors damaged several heritage structures.
2020.image: Photo: Taal Volcano and Taal Lake

1898.title: The Philippine Flag
1898.description: Taal-born Marcela Agoncillo sewed the first Philippine flag, unfurled at the declaration of independence in Kawit on June 12, 1898.

1754.title: The Great Eruption
1754.description: A months-long eruption of Taal Volcano destroyed the lakeshore town. Residents moved to Caysasay and later to the present site above Balayan Bay.
1754.image: Photo: Ruins of the old Taal church, San Nicolas

1732.title: Capital of Batangas
1732.description: Taal became the provincial capital and a busy lake and river port linking Taal Lake to Balayan Bay.

1572.title: Founding of Taal
1572.description: Augustinian friars founded Taal on April 26, 1572 as the first Christian mission in Batangas. In 1575 it moved to the edge of the lake.
1572.image: Photo: Basilica de San Martin de Tours

figures.marcela: Maker of the first Philippine flag
figures.felipe: Diplomat at the Treaty of Paris talks (1898)
figures.galicano: Co-founder of La Solidaridad, Governor of Batangas

paragraphs: Taal was founded in 1572 by Augustinian missionaries at Balangon, near the Pansipit River, and grew into a lake and river port. Its early parish counted Balayan and Bauan as mission stations.

In 1732 Taal became the capital of Batangas. The great eruption of 1754 devastated the lakeshore towns, forcing Taal to move toward Balayan Bay and the provincial capital to move to what is now Batangas City.

In the 19th and 20th centuries several towns, including Lemery, San Luis, San Nicolas and Santa Teresita, were formed from parts of Taal. Its sons and daughters, from the Agoncillos to Galicano Apacible, played a large part in the revolution and the early republic.

culture.seoDescription: Crafts, food, festivals and faith traditions of Taal, Batangas.
culture.title: Culture of Taal
culture.subtitle: Experience the embroidery, balisong, food and fiestas that make Taal the heritage capital of Batangas.

barong.title: Barong Tagalog and Burdang Taal
barong.text: Hand embroidery on piña and jusi fabric for barong and camisa, a home industry passed down for generations.

balisong.title: Balisong
balisong.text: The Filipino fan knife, crafted by hand in Taal, especially in Barangay Balisong.

cuisine.title: Cuisine
cuisine.text: Tapang Taal, longganisang Taal, empanada, sinaing na tulingan, adobo sa dilaw, suman and panutsa.

festivals.title: Festivals
festivals.text: The El Pasubat Festival every April and the town fiesta honoring St. Martin of Tours and Our Lady of Caysasay.

churches.title: Churches and Ancestral Houses
churches.text: The Basilica de San Martin de Tours, the Caysasay shrine and ancestral houses like the Marcela Agoncillo house, now a museum.

stMartin.name: Feast of St. Martin of Tours

caysasay.name: Feast of Our Lady of Caysasay

embroidery.name: Embroidery
embroidery.detail: Burdang Taal on piña and jusi

paragraphs: Taal is called the balisong and Barong Tagalog capital of the Philippines. Its embroiderers and knife makers keep crafts alive that started as home industries in the town.
The name El Pasubat comes from the things Taal is known for: empanada, longganisa, panutsa, suman, balisong, barong and tapa. Tamales, tawilis and tulingan were added later.
Faith is central to town life. The feasts of St. Martin of Tours and Our Lady of Caysasay bring processions and old traditions back to the streets each year.
Taal is divided into 42 barangays. Fourteen poblacion barangays make up the heritage town center, while the rest spread toward Taal Lake, the Pansipit River and Balayan Bay.
Each barangay is made up of puroks, and some have sitios. Barangay officials, contact details and health stations will be added to each barangay page.

about.title: About the Portal
about.subtitle: A volunteer-built guide to the services, offices and people of the Municipality of Taal, Batangas.

sections.title: What This Is
body: BetterTaalBatangas.org puts the information residents of Taal need most in one place: how to get a permit or certificate, what to bring, how much it costs, which office to go to, who our elected officials are and which numbers to call in an emergency.
Everything is written in plain language and organized around what people are trying to do, not around how the government is organized.

sections.title: Why We Built It
body: Government information is often scattered across Facebook posts, scanned documents and notices at the municipal hall. We believe that finding out how to register a birth or renew a business permit should take a minute, not a trip.
This portal is an act of civic service. It is built by volunteers who care about Taal, in their own time, at no cost to the people or the government of Taal.

sections.title: Not an Official Government Website
body: BetterTaalBatangas.org is not run by the Municipality of Taal or any government agency. We are independent volunteers. We cannot process applications, accept payments or answer for any office.

For official transactions, please visit the Taal Municipal Hall or contact the office concerned. Office emails are listed in the <gov>Government Directory</gov>, and emergency numbers are on the <hotlines>Hotlines</hotlines> page.

sections.title: Where the Information Comes From
body: Services, fees and offices: the {{charterTitle}} published by the Municipality of Taal.
Elected officials: the May 2025 election results and public records.
Weather: Open-Meteo.com.
Exchange rates: the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, through the BetterGov.ph API.
History and culture: published sources, credited on each page.
We check our work, but details can change before we catch them. When in doubt, confirm with the office concerned.

sections.title: Part of BetterGov.ph
body: This site is built on the open-source template of <bettergov>BetterGov.ph</bettergov>, a volunteer movement making Philippine government information easier to find and use. Many towns and cities now have their own Better LGU portal, each maintained by local volunteers.

sections.title: How You Can Help
body: Report errors. Found something wrong or out of date? Report an issue and we will correct it.
Share what you know. Barangay officials, updated fees and office hours are always welcome.
Contribute. The code is open on GitHub. Developers, designers, writers and translators can all help.
Spread the word. Share the site with family and neighbors who need it.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.subtitle: Reach the volunteers behind BetterTaalBatangas.org, or find the right office for official concerns.

sections.title: Report an Issue
body: Found something wrong or out of date? Tell us through our short report form: which page has the problem and what the correct information is, with a source if you have one.
Please do not include sensitive personal information such as ID numbers. We only need your contact details if you would like a reply.

sections.title: Email
body: You can also write to us at <contactEmail>{{contactEmail}}</contactEmail>. We are volunteers, so replies may take a few days.

sections.title: Official Municipal Concerns
body: We are not the Municipality of Taal and cannot process applications, payments, complaints or requests for documents. For these, please contact the municipal government directly:
Visit the Taal Municipal Hall, Taal, Batangas, during office hours.
Email the Office of the Mayor at <mayorEmail>{{mayorEmail}}</mayorEmail>.
Find the email of a specific office in the <offices>Government Directory</offices>.
For emergencies, see the <hotlines>Hotlines</hotlines> page.

sections.title: Volunteer With Us
body: Want to help keep this site accurate and useful? The project is open source on <repo>GitHub</repo>. You can suggest changes, fix content, improve the Tagalog translation or help with design and code.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers about who runs this site, where the information comes from and how to use it.

faq.q: Is this the official website of the Municipality of Taal?
faq.a: No. BetterTaalBatangas.org is an independent, volunteer-run portal. It is not operated or endorsed by the Municipality of Taal or any government agency.

faq.q: Who built and maintains this website?
faq.a: Volunteers from Taal and its friends, as part of the BetterGov.ph movement. Anyone can help; see the <about>About</about> page.
Volunteers cover the small costs, such as the domain. The site costs the people and the government of Taal nothing. We do not run ads or accept political funding.

faq.q: Does this website support any politician or party?
faq.a: No. The portal is non-partisan. Officials are listed because they hold office, not as an endorsement.

faq.q: Where does the information come from?
faq.a: Services, fees and offices come from the <charter>{{charterTitle}}</charter>. Officials come from the May 2025 election results. Weather comes from Open-Meteo, and exchange rates from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas.

faq.q: Is the information always up to date?
faq.a: We update it whenever we learn of changes, but fees, requirements and office hours can change without notice. Before you go, confirm with the office concerned.

faq.q: I found an error. What should I do?
faq.a: Please <report>report an issue</report> with the page, what is wrong and the correct information if you know it. We fix reports as soon as we can.

faq.q: Can I apply for a permit or pay fees here?
faq.a: No. This site explains how each service works, but all applications and payments are made at the municipal hall or through official channels.

faq.q: Can I reuse the content of this website?
faq.a: Yes. Our own content is public domain unless otherwise stated. Content from other sources, such as photos, belongs to their owners and is credited on each page.
No. There are no accounts or sign-ups. Everything is free to read.

faq.q: Does this website collect my personal information?
faq.a: No. We do not use analytics, ads or tracking cookies. See our <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> for the details.

faq.q: Is the website available in Tagalog?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Tagalog from the language menu at the top of any page. The detailed requirements and steps of each service stay in English, as printed in the official Citizen's Charter.

faq.q: Can I use this website on my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Every page works on phones, tablets and computers.
Report errors, share updated information or contribute on <repo>GitHub</repo>. Non-developers are welcome too.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.subtitle: The rules for using BetterTaalBatangas.org, a volunteer-run civic portal.

sections.title: Introduction
body: BetterTaalBatangas.org (“the portal”, “we”) is a free, community-run website that explains the services and offices of the Municipality of Taal, Batangas. These terms apply to everyone who uses it.

sections.title: Acceptance of Terms
body: By using the portal, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the portal.

sections.title: Not an Official Government Website
body: The portal is run by independent volunteers. It is not owned, operated or endorsed by the Municipality of Taal, the Province of Batangas or any government agency. Nothing on the portal is an official government statement, notice or decision.

sections.title: Content and License
body: Content we write is dedicated to the public domain unless otherwise stated. You may copy, share and reuse it freely.

Some content, such as photos and quoted material, belongs to others and is credited where it appears. Those works remain under their owners’ terms. The source code is available on <repo>GitHub</repo> under its stated license.

sections.title: "As Is" Disclaimer
body: We work to keep the portal accurate, but it is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind. Fees, requirements, schedules and officials can change without notice. Always confirm important details with the office concerned before acting on them.

sections.title: Limitation of Liability
body: To the extent allowed by law, the volunteers behind the portal are not liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of, or reliance on, the portal or the sites it links to.

sections.title: Your Responsibilities
body: Use the portal lawfully and in good faith.
Do not try to disrupt, overload or gain unauthorized access to the portal.
Do not present the portal’s content as an official government statement.
When reporting errors, share accurate information and do not post anyone’s personal data.

sections.title: No Professional Advice
body: The portal gives general information only. It is not legal, financial, medical or other professional advice. For advice on your situation, consult a qualified professional or the office concerned.

sections.title: External Links
body: The portal links to government websites, data sources and other sites we do not control. We are not responsible for their content, availability or privacy practices.

sections.title: Availability
body: As a volunteer project, the portal may be changed, paused or discontinued at any time without notice.

sections.title: Changes to These Terms
body: We may update these terms. The date at the bottom of this page shows the latest version. Continuing to use the portal means you accept the updated terms.

sections.title: Governing Law
body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Philippines.

sections.title: Contact
body: Questions about these terms? See the <contact>Contact Us</contact> page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: We collect as little as possible. Here is exactly what happens when you use BetterTaalBatangas.org.

sections.title: Introduction
body: BetterTaalBatangas.org is a volunteer-run information portal. We respect your privacy and follow the principles of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173): collect only what is needed, use it only for a clear purpose and keep it safe.

sections.title: Our Approach
body: No accounts, sign-ups or log-ins.
No forms that collect personal information.
No analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
We never sell or rent information about our visitors.

sections.title: Information That Is Processed
body: On your device. If you change the language, your choice is saved in your browser’s local storage so the site remembers it. It never leaves your device, and you can clear it in your browser settings.

By our hosting provider. Like any website, the server that delivers our pages may record basic technical data, such as your IP address, browser type and the pages requested, for security and to keep the site running.

By services that supply content. To show fonts, weather and exchange rates, your browser loads data from Google Fonts, Open-Meteo and the BetterGov.ph API. These services receive your IP address as part of the request and handle it under their own privacy policies.

sections.title: When You Contact Us
body: If you use our report form, your answers are collected through Google Forms and handled under Google’s privacy policy. Only the volunteers who maintain the portal can see them. We use what you send only to correct and improve the portal. If you email us, we use your message and address only to reply and to improve the portal, and we do not share them. Please do not send sensitive personal information.

sections.title: Cookies
body: We do not set cookies. The only thing we store is the language preference described above.

sections.title: Data Security
body: The portal is a static website served over HTTPS. Because we do not keep a database of visitor information, there is very little personal data to protect or to lose.

sections.title: Your Rights
body: Under the Data Privacy Act, you have the right to be informed, to access, to correct and to erase your personal data, and to object to its processing. To exercise these rights for any message you sent us, see the <contact>Contact Us</contact> page.
You may also file a complaint with the <npc>National Privacy Commission</npc>.

sections.title: Children's Privacy
body: The portal is for the general public and does not knowingly collect information from children.

sections.title: Third-Party Links
body: We link to government and other websites. Their privacy practices are their own, so please review their policies.

sections.title: Changes to This Policy
body: If our practices change, for example if we ever add analytics, we will update this page first. The date below shows the latest version.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.subtitle: Government information should be usable by everyone in Taal, including seniors and people with disabilities.

sections.title: Our Commitment
body: We aim for BetterTaalBatangas.org to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA. We check pages as we build them and fix problems as we find them.

sections.title: What We Do
body: Readable text: body text is at least 14 pixels, and text and background colors meet WCAG AA contrast.
Plain language: steps, requirements and fees are written simply and laid out one item per line.
Keyboard friendly: menus, links and buttons can be used without a mouse, with a visible focus outline.
Screen reader support: pages use proper headings, labels and text alternatives for icons and images.
Any screen size: every page works on phones, tablets and computers, and with browser zoom.
Two languages: every page can be read in English or Tagalog.
Light pages: no autoplaying media and no heavy downloads, so pages load on slow connections.

sections.title: Known Limitations
body: Some documents we link to, such as the Citizen’s Charter, are scanned PDFs published by the municipality and may not work with screen readers.
The detailed requirements and steps of each service are in English only, as printed in the official Citizen’s Charter.
Content from other services, such as weather and exchange rates, depends on those providers.

sections.title: Alternative Access
body: If you cannot use part of this site, the same information is available from the office concerned at the Taal Municipal Hall. Office emails are listed in the <offices>Government Directory</offices>.

sections.title: Feedback
body: If something is hard to read or use, please tell us through the <contact>Contact Us</contact> page. Include the page and what went wrong, and we will work on a fix.
